chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Haysam ibn Abi Masrouq, from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Bazi'e, from Ahmad ibn A'aiz, from Kuleyb Al-Saydawi, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Supplicate to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for me regarding livelihood, for my affairs have worsened upon me.' So he answered quickly, 'Go out and seek.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on seeking livelihood and the role of supplication?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Kuleyb Al-Saydawi requests a supplication for relief from financial distress, to which Imam Al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) responds with the concise directive 'Do not go out, seek' (or 'Go out and seek'), highlighting the Shia principle that divine supplication must be coupled with active effort (*al-ibda'*). This narration underscores the balance between reliance on God (*tawakkul*) and the obligation of personal initiative in securing livelihood, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence and ethics.
